The core operator is a random forest classifier (RF) that estimates pass completion probability per frame using 16 tracking features. It achieves high AUC (0.8829) via 10-fold leave-group-out CV, indicating strong discriminative power. Conditional calibration (Pearson 0.998) validates the reliability of P(C|T=i) per frame. However, marginal accuracy (95.8%) is misleading due to class imbalance. The model's design assumes frame-level geometric data availability, which is not present in PBP-only datasets. This creates a dualism between frame-level inference (GSE) and play-level prediction (nflfastR cp). The failure mode occurs when attempting to apply frame-level models to play-grain data without geometric context.
